cohort_name: OPUS trial
diagnostic_instrument: ICD-10 F20 F22-F25 F28-F29; SCAN 2.1 interview
diagnosis_confirmed: clinical interview by trained staff
overlap_notes: hansen2024 and hansen2024b are the same OPUS participants; hansen2024 uses the 496 FEP schizophrenia sample (F21 excluded) and hansen2024b the 578 spectrum sample (F21 included)
employment_selection_verbatim: Participants were between 18 and 45 years old at the time of inclusion. They had been diagnosed with a first episode of schizophrenia spectrum disorders (F20, F22-25, F28-29) according to the International Classification of Diseases, 10th revision (ICD-10). Participants were excluded if they had received more than 3 months of treatment with antipsychotics before study inclusion. | Corroborated (hansen2024b, p. 2564): 'Participants were between 18 and 45 years of age and had not received more than 12 weeks of consecutive antipsychotic treatment.' Baseline employment was measured, not required: 'Working or studying 126 (30.3)' at baseline (Table 2, p. 4379), so 70% were not working or studying at entry and were retained.
employment_selection_source: hansen2024, Methods, Study population and design, p. 4375; corroborated hansen2024b, Method, Settings, p. 2564

cohort_name: Northern Finland Birth Cohort 1966
diagnostic_instrument: register diagnosis ICD-8 ICD-9 ICD-10
diagnosis_confirmed: register diagnosis only; no clinical re-interview
overlap_notes: rautio2016 and majuri2021 are the same birth cohort but different case sets; majuri2021 analyses only the disability-pension subgroup
employment_selection_verbatim: This study is based on the NFBC 1966 study, which is a general population cohort study concerning 12,068 pregnant women and their 12,058 live-born children in 1966 in the provinces of Oulu and Lapland. This study includes individuals who were alive at the age of 16 years and living in Finland (n = 11,017) ... leading to a sample of 10,277. | Diagnosis of SSD was based on an individual's presence in the national register from 1982 to 2006 ... as well as follow-up of at least five years since the age of illness onset. | Corroborated (majuri2021, p. 1646): 'an unselected, general population sample based on 12,058 live-born children'.
employment_selection_source: rautio2016, Methods 2.1 Sample, p. 63; corroborated majuri2021, Methods, Sample, p. 1646

cohort_name: State Hospital Survey (Carstairs) 1992-93 cohort
diagnostic_instrument: St Louis (Feighner) criteria; case note review plus clinical interview
diagnosis_confirmed: definite or probable schizophrenia by Feighner criteria for the 169 subgroup
overlap_notes: thomson2023 follows the whole 241-patient cohort; darjee2017 follows the 169 with schizophrenia from the same survey
employment_selection_verbatim: A cohort of 169 patients ... with schizophrenia resident in the high-security State Hospital in Scotland, UK between 25 August 1992 and 13 August 1993, were identified from the 241 patients detained there at that time ... All patients had committed acts of serious violence and were admitted from criminal courts, less secure hospitals or from prison. | Corroborated (thomson2023, p. 3): 'a whole population cohort of 241 patients ... detained within the high secure State Hospital, Carstairs, Scotland'. Baseline employment was recorded, not required: 'Employment status when last in community - Employed 50 (29.6); Unemployed 119 (70.4)' (darjee2017 Table 1, p. 531).
employment_selection_source: darjee2017, Methods, Sample, p. 526; corroborated thomson2023, Methods, Sample, p. 3

cohort_name: Improving Social Recovery in Early Psychosis (ISREP) trial
diagnostic_instrument: not stated in this report
diagnosis_confirmed: not stated in this report
overlap_notes: 2-year follow-up of the ISREP MRC trial platform study
employment_selection_verbatim: Eligibility required being currently unemployed or engaged in fewer than 16 hours per week of paid employment or education. PROVENANCE: this criterion is NOT stated in fowler2019, the report held in this repository, which gives no eligibility criteria and defers to Fowler et al. 2009b, Psychol Med 39:1627-1636. The criterion was supplied by the authorship group on 12 Aug 2026 from the ISREP primary analysis via Cambridge Core, corroborated by the original trial report's account of recruitment on a history of unemployment and poor social outcome. Fowler 2009b is paywalled and NOT held here, so the exact printed wording is pending documentary confirmation when that paper is obtained.
employment_selection_source: Authorship-group adjudication 12 Aug 2026, citing the ISREP primary analysis (Fowler et al. 2009b, Psychol Med 39:1627-1636). Not verifiable against any PDF currently held.

cohort_name: IPS trial NCT01722344 Copenhagen Odense and Silkeborg
diagnostic_instrument: ICD-10 F20-F29 F31 F33 confirmed with SCAN
diagnosis_confirmed: diagnostic interview (SCAN) by trained certified researcher
overlap_notes: DREAM register outcome data so may overlap with whole-population Danish register studies of 2012-2017
employment_selection_verbatim: Participants were eligible if they had a diagnosis of schizophrenia, schizotypal disorder, delusional disorder (ICD-10 F20-F29); bipolar disorder (F31); or recurrent depression (F33). All participants were adults (aged 18-64 years) living in 1 of 3 Danish cities ... All were assigned to early-intervention teams or community mental health services. ALL ELIGIBLE PARTICIPANTS EXPRESSED A CLEAR DESIRE IN COMPETITIVE EMPLOYMENT OR EDUCATION and spoke and understood Danish sufficiently well to participate without an interpreter. | NOT baseline unemployment: work history was a STRATIFICATION variable and Table 1 (p. 1236) shows roughly half of each arm had 2+ months of paid work in the previous 5 years. Additionally 100% of each arm sat in Danish labour-market match group 2 or 3, a work-capability classification (Table 1 footnote f).
employment_selection_source: christensen2019, Methods, Eligibility Criteria, p. 1233

cohort_name: unnamed: New Zealand national FEP cohort (Statistics NZ Integrated Data Infrastructure), 2009-2012
diagnostic_instrument: ICD-10 and DSM-IV codes recorded in specialist mental health service data (Supplementary Table 2)
diagnosis_confirmed: register/clinical service diagnosis; multiple diagnoses over 5 years prioritised to one per person
overlap_notes: Same IDI FEP cohort as Petrovic-van der Deen et al. 2020 Schizophr Res 223:311-8; Manuel et al. 2022 ANZJP; Carr et al. Early Interv Psychiatry. All counts randomly rounded to base 3 by Stats NZ
employment_selection_verbatim: We previously identified a retrospective cohort of 2412 13- to 25-year-old individuals diagnosed with FEP between 2009 and 2012. To develop this cohort we used health record data (specifically specialist mental health service use and diagnosis data) held in the Statistics New Zealand Integrated Data Infrastructure (IDI) to identify individuals with a first recorded diagnosis of psychosis between the ages of 13 and 25 during the study period. | Exclusions: We excluded cohort members who had spent more than a quarter of the follow-up period (the 5 years post diagnosis) abroad or who had died during this period.
employment_selection_source: Method, Study population, pp. 1-2

cohort_name: unnamed: Danish national registers incident schizophrenia spectrum cohort, 1998-2023
diagnostic_instrument: ICD-10 F20-F29 first-time diagnosis in the Danish National Patient Register
diagnosis_confirmed: register diagnosis; no clinical re-verification
overlap_notes: Danish national registers; overlaps Sturup et al. 2023 and other DREAM/NPR studies and will include OPUS trial participants. Counts rounded under Statistics Denmark disclosure rules
employment_selection_verbatim: The source population included all individuals residing in Denmark who received a first-time diagnosis of a nonaffective psychotic disorder (ICD-10 codes F20-F29). The date of the first registered F20-F29 diagnosis was defined as the cohort entry date. To ensure complete temporal alignment between medication exposure and employment data, we restricted the cohort to individuals with index diagnosis dates between January 1, 1998, and December 31, 2023 ... Individuals were excluded if they died or emigrated within 2 years of cohort entry.
employment_selection_source: Methods, Study population, p. 2

cohort_name: Bologna West First Episode Psychosis project (Bo-FEP)
diagnostic_instrument: Item Group Checklist of SCAN version 2.1 completed from case notes; psychosis per APA 2004 criteria
diagnosis_confirmed: case-note IGC ratings discussed with the treating psychiatrists
overlap_notes: Same incidence cohort as Tarricone et al. 2012 Psychol Med (8-year Bo-FEP incidence study). Recruitment was catchment-based at Bologna West CMHCs which run a first-episode programme; setting coded community_smh rather than eip
employment_selection_verbatim: This study is part of the Bologna West First Episode Psychosis project (Bo-FEP), an incidence FEP study of all patients between 18 and 64 years, who had a contact with Bologna West Community Mental Health Centers (CMHCs) from January 2002 to December 2009. | We carried out a 12 months follow-up of all first episode psychosis patients identified in the study period.
employment_selection_source: Methods, Setting and service description, p. 522; Study design, p. 523

cohort_name: unnamed: 16 centres, Croatia, 2007-2009 (risperidone long-acting injection observational study)
diagnostic_instrument: DSM-IV and ICD-10 criteria for schizophrenia schizoaffective disorder or other psychotic disorder
diagnosis_confirmed: clinician diagnosis at 16 participating centres
overlap_notes: Janssen-funded single-arm naturalistic RLAI study. Croatia coded europe_south per UN M49; europe_east is equally defensible. perc_qualifying_diagnosis 100 per the Table 1 footnote, but the Table 4/5 footnote lists F31 and F32 under Other, which would put it below 100 | RECRUITMENT is unselected; the employment-related restriction attaches to the pension_excluded ANALYSIS UNIT, not to the recruited cohort. Corrected 12 Aug 2026 on authorship-group adjudication.
employment_selection_verbatim: Both, inpatients and outpatients were considered, as long as a change in treatment was indicated. Patients were included irrespective of the reason for the treatment change (e.g. lack of response, side effects, etc.). Eligible patients were aged 18 years or older, met criteria of DSM-IV and ICD-10 for schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder or other psychotic disorder, and signed an informed consent document for participation in the study. Patients were enrolled from 16 centres in Croatia, from June, 2007 until February, 2009. Excluded were patients who had a known hypersensitivity to risperidone.
employment_selection_source: Subjects and Methods, Subjects, p. 264

cohort_name: unnamed: community rehabilitation centre attached to Kai-Syuan Psychiatric Hospital, southern Taiwan, 2021
diagnostic_instrument: not stated; pre-existing clinical diagnosis of schizophrenia
diagnosis_confirmed: not stated
overlap_notes: Whole sample was already in one of three vocational training placements at baseline by design, so the employment distribution is a property of the selected sample and not of a clinical population
employment_selection_verbatim: The criteria for acceptance were PwS who (i) had been diagnosed, (ii) were first undergoing vocational training less than 3 months, (iii) could communicate in Chinese or Taiwanese Hokkien, and (iv) were conscious and able to express their personal opinions. | The participants were from a community rehabilitation center attached to a psychiatric hospital in southern Taiwan that provides vocational training. | For the study's baseline, 14, 31, and 20 participants were in supported employment, sheltered employment, and unpaid job training, respectively.
employment_selection_source: Methods, Study Design and Participants, pp. 167-168; Results, Participants, pp. 170-171

cohort_name: unnamed: Asia-Pacific 18-month open-label PP1M study (NCT01051531), 8 countries
diagnostic_instrument: DSM-IV-TR schizophrenia diagnosed within the previous 5 years
diagnosis_confirmed: trial eligibility assessment by site investigators
overlap_notes: Post-hoc analysis of NCT01051531; primary results Zhang et al. 2015 and Taiwan subgroup Tang et al. 2019. Income level is mixed: upper-middle 264 patients (China 106, Malaysia 109, Thailand 49), high 205 (Korea 81, Taiwan 60, Australia 46, Hong Kong 18), lower-middle 5 (Philippines); coded to the modal category. Recruitment years not reported in this paper
employment_selection_verbatim: Eligible patients were aged 18-50 years old and diagnosed with schizophrenia within the past 5 years (DSM-IV-TR criteria) ... Patients were enrolled after unsuccessful treatment with prior antipsychotics due to inefficacy, poor tolerability, safety issues, or non-compliance. Exclusions included treatment-resistant schizophrenia, medication-induced psychiatric disorders, recent substance use disorder, or clozapine/LAI use.
employment_selection_source: Methods 2.2 Patient population, p. 2

cohort_name: unnamed: University Psychiatry Unit, National Hospital of Sri Lanka, first episode cohort (FEC), 2016-2019
diagnostic_instrument: ICD-10 Research Diagnostic Criteria
diagnosis_confirmed: diagnosis confirmed by the principal investigator a consultant psychiatrist
overlap_notes: Split from the former single cohort `nhsl_colombo` on 11 Aug 2026. The FEC and REC are prospectively defined, mutually exclusive samples with separate a-priori sample-size targets ('The required sample size was 115 per cohort', Methods 2.2, p. 2), so they cannot share participants and are two cohorts rather than two subgroup arms.
employment_selection_verbatim: We recruited participants aged 15-60 years with a diagnosis of schizophrenia according to ICD-10 Research Diagnostic Criteria (World Health Organization, 1993) from inpatient and outpatient services. | We excluded patients with substance induced psychosis, schizoaffective disorder, other primary psychotic disorders, or significant organic brain disease (including alcohol-related brain damage, dementia, delirium, or intellectual disability). We included those with other psychiatric or medical comorbidities. | The first episode cohort (FEC) included patients presenting for the first time to mental health services with a duration of untreated psychosis (DUP) under 12 months, without a period of remission in between, with sustained psychotic symptoms >=1 week.
employment_selection_source: Methods 2.1 Study design and setting, 2.2 Inclusion and exclusion criteria, 2.3 First episode and relapsing cohorts, all p. 2

cohort_name: unnamed: University Psychiatry Unit, National Hospital of Sri Lanka, recurrent/relapsing episode cohort (REC), 2016-2019
diagnostic_instrument: ICD-10 Research Diagnostic Criteria
diagnosis_confirmed: diagnosis confirmed by the principal investigator a consultant psychiatrist
overlap_notes: Split from the former single cohort `nhsl_colombo` on 11 Aug 2026. The FEC and REC are prospectively defined, mutually exclusive samples with separate a-priori sample-size targets ('The required sample size was 115 per cohort', Methods 2.2, p. 2), so they cannot share participants and are two cohorts rather than two subgroup arms.
employment_selection_verbatim: We recruited participants aged 15-60 years with a diagnosis of schizophrenia according to ICD-10 Research Diagnostic Criteria (World Health Organization, 1993) from inpatient and outpatient services. | We excluded patients with substance induced psychosis, schizoaffective disorder, other primary psychotic disorders, or significant organic brain disease (including alcohol-related brain damage, dementia, delirium, or intellectual disability). We included those with other psychiatric or medical comorbidities. | The recurrent/relapsing episode cohort (REC) comprised patients with a prior diagnosis of schizophrenia presenting with a new episode or relapse.
employment_selection_source: Methods 2.1 Study design and setting, 2.2 Inclusion and exclusion criteria, 2.3 First episode and relapsing cohorts, all p. 2

cohort_name: EASY programme early intervention cohort, Hong Kong (1 July 2001 to 30 June 2002 entrants)
diagnostic_instrument: ICD-10 (1992) clinical diagnosis at service entry; longitudinal DSM-IV Axis I diagnosis at 10 years
diagnosis_confirmed: baseline diagnosis determined by clinicians using ICD-10 criteria and all available clinical information; re-reviewed at 10 years against DSM-IV using clinical interview and medical records, and non-schizophrenia-spectrum cases excluded
overlap_notes: One recruited sample of 148 consecutive EASY entrants with a schizophrenia-spectrum diagnosis, described by chan2019, by the early intervention group of chan2020 and by the EIS group of chan2022. Individually matched to the separately recruited historical control cohort hk_standard_care_2000. Near-certain participant overlap with hk_easy_fep_2001_2003 (chang2016), whose EASY enrolment window July 2001 to August 2003 contains this one; neither report states the overlap, so results from the two cohorts must never be pooled. NO EMPLOYMENT COUNT is recoverable from any of the three reports describing this cohort.
employment_selection_verbatim: Consecutive patients who received the EI service in the whole region of Hong Kong between 1st July 2001 and 30th June 2002 and with a diagnosis of schizophrenia-spectrum disorder were identified from the centralized hospital database (Clinical Management system, CMS). Patients with comorbid organic brain conditions, drug-induced psychosis, learning disabilities or had more than one month of prior psychiatric treatment before presentation were excluded. There were 148 patients identified. | Corroborated (chan2020, p. 492): 'We excluded patients with comorbid organic brain conditions, drug-induced psychosis, intellectual disabilities and those who had received prior psychiatric treatment for longer than 1 month before presentation to the early intervention service.' Eligibility is fully enumerated in both reports and contains no employment-related criterion; EASY is a region-wide service taking all patients aged 15-25 with first-episode psychosis.
employment_selection_source: chan2019, Methods 2.2 Sample, p. 66; corroborated chan2020, Method, Samples, p. 492 and chan2022, Methods 2.1, p. 2

cohort_name: Hong Kong standard care historical control cohort (1 July 2000 to 30 June 2001 first presenters)
diagnostic_instrument: ICD-10 (1992) clinical diagnosis at first presentation; longitudinal DSM-IV Axis I diagnosis at 10 years
diagnosis_confirmed: same ascertainment as hk_easy_2001; longitudinal DSM-IV review at 10 years with non-schizophrenia-spectrum cases excluded
overlap_notes: Second, separately recruited sample described by chan2020 and chan2022, recorded as its own cohort under D12.5 and codebook rule 11: a different service (publicly funded psychiatric out-patient and in-patient care with no dedicated case manager) and a recruitment window one year earlier than hk_easy_2001, individually matched pair by pair. It is not a subgroup of hk_easy_2001. No employment count is recoverable from either report.
employment_selection_verbatim: We individually matched the identified patients - based on gender, age at presentation and diagnosis at onset - with those who first presented to the standard care service between 1 July 2000 and 30 June 2001. The same inclusion and exclusion criteria applied to the standard care group. | The standard service consisted of publicly funded psychiatric out-patient clinic consultation and in-patient care. Matching and eligibility are on gender, age at presentation and diagnosis only; no employment-related criterion appears in either report.
employment_selection_source: chan2020, Method, Study setting and Samples, p. 492; corroborated chan2022, Methods 2.1, p. 2

cohort_name: EASY programme first-episode psychosis outcome study cohort, Hong Kong (July 2001 to August 2003 entrants)
diagnostic_instrument: ICD-10 (1992) criteria; final 3-year clinical ICD-10 research diagnosis taking the longitudinal course of the illness into account
diagnosis_confirmed: clinical ICD-10 diagnosis ascertained at 3 years by systematic medical record review with standardised data-entry forms, weekly consensus meetings and satisfactory inter-rater reliability (ICC 0.70 to 1.00) for DUP and major outcome measures
overlap_notes: NEW COHORT, split out of hk_easy_2001 during batch F01. 700 patients enrolled in EASY July 2001 to August 2003; 515 diagnosed with schizophrenia or first-episode mania with psychotic features; 420 completed 3-year follow-up (374 schizophrenia, 46 psychotic mania). This is a different recruited sample from hk_easy_2001 (wider window, and first-episode mania with psychotic features included), and it near-certainly contains the hk_easy_2001 participants; recorded as overlaps_with in report_cohort_map.csv. Results from this cohort must never be pooled with any hk_easy_2001 result. Diagnosis group is psychosis_mixed because 11.0% of the analysed sample had first-episode mania with psychotic features; the schizophrenia subgroup is separately extractable.
employment_selection_verbatim: The current report was part of a large-scale first-episode psychosis (FEP) outcome study comprising 700 patients enrolled in the Early Assessment Service for Young People with Psychosis (EASY) from July 2001 to August 2003. EASY is a territory-wide, publicly-funded early intervention program for individuals aged 15-25 years presenting with FEP in Hong Kong. | Patients who had mental retardation, psychotic disorders due to general medical condition, substance-induced psychosis or received psychiatric treatment for more than 1 month before service entry were excluded. Eligibility is fully enumerated and contains no employment-related criterion; entry is by presentation with first-episode psychosis to a territory-wide service, not by vocational status, work intention or vocational-service referral.
employment_selection_source: chang2016, Methods 2.1 Participants, p. 2

cohort_name: Extended early intervention randomised controlled trial, Hong Kong (EASY 2-year completers)
diagnostic_instrument: DSM-IV; Chinese-bilingual Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-IV (CB-SCID), informant histories and medical records
diagnosis_confirmed: research interview (CB-SCID) supplemented by informant history and medical records
overlap_notes: NEW COHORT, split out of hk_easy_2001 during batch F01. Randomised trial sample of 160 patients (extended EI 82, step-down care 78) recruited AFTER completing the 2-year EASY programme, analysed on the 156 with completed follow-up assessments. Not the hk_easy_2001 sample: entry required 2 years of prior EASY treatment, recruitment dates are not stated in this report, and the service is described here as five clinical teams against four in chan2019/chan2020. Overlap with any other cohort cannot be established from this report and is therefore not asserted.
employment_selection_verbatim: A total of 160 patients with a DSM-IV diagnosis of psychotic disorder were recruited from EASY program, randomly allocated to Extended EI (n = 82) or SC (n = 78), and followed up for 12 months. Exclusion criteria were intellectual disability, substance-induced psychosis or psychotic disorder due to general medical condition. | The stated exclusion criteria carry no employment-related restriction, but this report does not give its own full eligibility criteria: 'Details of the study methodology have been reported elsewhere (Chang et al., 2015).' Under D9 silence in an incompletely reported methods section is `unclear`, not `none`. Entry did require completion of 2 years of EASY treatment, which is a service-participation restriction, though not an employment-related one on the wording available.
employment_selection_source: chang2016b, Methods 2.1 Subjects and setting, p. 80

cohort_name: Job Management Programme (JUMP)
diagnostic_instrument: M.I.N.I. PLUS (Norwegian version, modules A, C, D, K, L, M); DSM-IV broad schizophrenia spectrum disorder
diagnosis_confirmed: diagnostic interview at baseline by clinicians trained in the instrument
overlap_notes: Five reports on one cohort of 148 starters. evensen2017 and gjerdalen2023 report the whole 148; evensen2019 the 69 who consented to register extraction; lystad2017 and klungsyr2021 the 131 who completed neurocognitive assessment. Six counties, three randomised to CR and three to CBT; no non-augmented control arm existed ('A control group without the augmentation proved impossible to include', klungsyr2021, Sample, p. 3). ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01139502.
employment_selection_verbatim: RECRUITMENT INTO A VOCATIONAL SERVICE: 'Participants were recruited from local mental health centres and vocational services within the six catchment areas. Self-referral was also possible.' (evensen2017, Participants, p. 181); 'Participants were recruited from within the mental health services, NAV, and through self-referral in the six counties that were involved in the JUMP study.' (evensen2019, Participants, p. 2; NAV is the Norwegian Labour and Welfare Administration). | COHORT MEMBERSHIP REQUIRED STARTING THE VOCATIONAL REHABILITATION: 'A total of 319 persons were referred to the JUMP study. Of these, 76 did not meet the inclusion criteria and 61 declined, mainly due to lack of motivation, poor timing, or reluctance to participate in research. Another nine did not complete the assessments, and 25 did not start the vocational rehabilitation after assessment. The remaining 148 participants were included in the study between August 2009 and March 2012' (evensen2017, p. 182); Figure 1 prints '173 Eligible / 25 non-starters' feeding '148 starters' (p. 182). | WORK MOTIVATION ASSERTED OF THE WHOLE SAMPLE: 'In this study, where all the participants exhibited some level of motivation to work, those with the best requirements, showed the highest probability of obtaining employment.' (gjerdalen2023, Discussion, p. 28). | NOT baseline unemployment: the listed inclusion criteria are 'age between 18-65 years, an IQ above 70, a diagnosis within the [DSM-IV] criteria for a broad schizophrenia spectrum disorder, and adequate understanding of the Norwegian language' (evensen2017, p. 182) and contain no employment condition, and 'At the start of the intervention all participants were reliant on social security benefits, and 17% had some form of employment' (evensen2017, Background, p. 181), so being wholly out of work was not required.
employment_selection_source: evensen2017, Materials and methods / Participants, pp. 181-182 and Figure 1, p. 182; evensen2019, Methods / Participants, p. 2 and Fig. 1, p. 3; gjerdalen2023, Methods 2.3 Participants, pp. 24-25 and Discussion, p. 28

cohort_name: PAFIP (Programa Asistencial Fases Iniciales de Psicosis), Cantabria
diagnostic_instrument: DSM-IV (APA, 2000) brief psychotic disorder, schizophreniform disorder, schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder; Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-IV (SCID-I)
diagnosis_confirmed: SCID-I administered by the same senior consultant psychiatrist six months after the baseline visit; diagnostic stability reviewed at the 10-year reassessment (ayesaarriola2020, Methods, Clinical and functional instruments, p. 6)
overlap_notes: Recruitment years are those of PAFIP-10 (referrals between February 2001 and December 2008, ayesaarriola2020, Methods, Study design and setting, p. 6). PAFIP itself is described as ongoing and mayoralvanson2019 does not state which years its 157-patient subsample covers, so its window may be narrower or wider. ayesaarriola2020 analyses 307 baseline and 209 reassessed patients; mayoralvanson2019 analyses 157. The overlap between the two analysed samples is not stated.
employment_selection_verbatim: 'The PAFIP-10 sample comprised all referrals to PAFIP between 2001 and 2008 that had been screened against the following inclusion criteria: age 15-60 years; living in the catchment area; experiencing their first episode of psychosis; no prior treatment with antipsychotic medication or, if previously treated, a total life time of adequate antipsychotic treatment of <6 weeks; meeting DSM-IV criteria (APA, 2000) for brief psychotic disorder, schizophreniform disorder, schizophrenia, or schizoaffective disorder. DSM-IV criteria for drug or alcohol dependence, intellectual disability, and having a history of neurological disease or head injury were exclusion criteria.' No criterion refers to employment, unemployment, wanting or being ready to work, an employment goal, vocational-service eligibility, a placement or previous employment failure. The programme is catchment-based: 'incidence and 10-year follow-up studies, respectively, of all individuals with an FEP presenting for the first time to mental health specialists in the catchment area of Cantabria'. Employment was measured at entry, not required: 69 of 156 were unemployed and 30 inactive at baseline (mayoralvanson2019, Table 3, p. 1186).
employment_selection_source: ayesaarriola2020, Methods, Subjects, p. 6, and Methods, Study design and setting, p. 6. mayoralvanson2019 does not restate the criteria: 'Both inclusion and exclusion criteria have also been described elsewhere (15)' (Methods 2.2 Subjects, p. 1183), so the cohort-level decision rests on ayesaarriola2020. The analysis-sample decision for mayoralvanson2019's 157 is recorded separately as analysis_selection_status = unclear in extraction_arms.

cohort_name: OnTrackNY coordinated specialty care programme, New York State
diagnostic_instrument: Clinician diagnosis of primary nonaffective psychosis with onset less than two years before enrolment; no structured research instrument
diagnosis_confirmed: 'Licensed team clinicians conducted a nonstandardized interview at intake. Because the goal of the interview was to establish a diagnosis of primary, nonaffective psychosis to determine eligibility, clinicians received training in differential diagnosis.' (nossel2018, Methods, Measures, p. 864). Diagnosis is programme-assigned and not independently verified.
overlap_notes: nossel2018 covers enrolments October 2013 to August 2016 at 10 sites (325 clients); basaraba2023 covers October 2013 to December 2018 at 20 sites (1298 clients) and therefore contains nossel2018's sample. Results from the two reports describe overlapping participants.
employment_selection_verbatim: 'The total sample included individuals ages 16 to 30 who had experienced nonaffective psychosis for less than two years, were enrolled at one of 10 OnTrackNY sites, and had completed at least one three-month follow-up assessment.' (nossel2018). 'The OnTrackNY program, a network of CSC sites in New York State, provides person-centered, recovery-oriented, and evidence-based psychosocial and pharmaceutical interventions to individuals aged 16 to 30 years with recent-onset (<2 years) nonaffective psychosis.' (basaraba2023). No eligibility criterion refers to employment status, wanting or readiness to work, an employment goal, vocational-service eligibility, a placement or previous employment failure; 56 per cent of the 325 were in neither work nor school at admission (nossel2018, Table 1, p. 865) and were retained. NOTE AS PROVENANCE, NOT SELECTION: the OnTrackNY service model itself includes 'a supported education and employment specialist' on every team, so care received is employment-supporting; entry to the service is not conditional on any employment criterion.
employment_selection_source: nossel2018, Methods, Participants and Study Design, p. 864, and Intervention, p. 864; corroborated by basaraba2023, Design Setting and Participants, p. 49, and Introduction, p. 50.

cohort_name: US Veterans Health Administration schizophrenia cohort (VHA Corporate Data Warehouse, 2013-2019)
diagnostic_instrument: Two or more administrative diagnosis records on different days: ICD-9-CM 295.xx, ICD-10-CM F20.x, F21 or F25.x, in any position
diagnosis_confirmed: Administrative diagnosis codes only; no clinical interview, chart review or validation of the codes is reported in either report.
overlap_notes: One source cohort of 119,343 veterans, reported twice. lin2022 propensity-matches 102,207 of them to non-schizophrenia veterans; benson2022 splits the same 119,343 into 16,866 with and 102,477 without a relapse in the 12-month pre-index period and propensity-matches 16,862 from each. The analysed samples of the two reports overlap by an unquantified but large amount and are not independent.
employment_selection_verbatim: Selection is given in full as a flow chart in both reports and contains no employment-related step: 'two or more records on different days with a diagnosis for schizophrenia (ICD-9-CM: 295.xx; ICD-10-CM: F20.x, F21, F25.x) in any position during the study period (January 1, 2013-September 30, 2019)'; 'one or more record with a diagnosis for schizophrenia in any position during the patient selection window (January 1, 2014-September 30, 2019)'; 'Enrolled in VHA benefits for minimum of 12 months prior to the index date'; 'one or more record (any medical and pharmacy benefit record) during the 12-month preindex period and at any time after the index date'; plus, in lin2022, 'Age >=18 years on the index date' and 'No missing data for age, gender, or region; region not outside the US; no other data quality issues'. Employment status is an outcome obtained by record linkage, not an entry criterion.
employment_selection_source: benson2022, Figure 1 'Patient Selection Criteria Flowchart' (PDF p. 6) and Methods, Study Design; lin2022, Figure 1 'Patient selection criteria and attrition', p. 3, and Methods, Study design, p. 3.

cohort_name: EPPIC individual placement and support randomised controlled trial (ACTRN12608000094370)
diagnostic_instrument: DSM-IV-TR first-episode psychosis; Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-IV-TR Axis I Disorders - Patient Edition (SCID-I/P)
diagnosis_confirmed: structured clinical interview (SCID-I/P) at baseline
overlap_notes: Described by killackey2019 (parent trial) and clarke2023 (secondary quality-of-life analysis). Recruitment is stated only as 'Recruitment occurred over a 3-year period' (killackey2019, Method, Trial design, p. 76); no calendar years are given in either report, so recruitment_start and recruitment_end are left blank.
employment_selection_verbatim: killackey2019: "Young people with FEP who had expressed an interest in vocational recovery were approached to participate." clarke2023: "Further inclusion criterion ensured participants had at least 6-months left in the EPPIC programme and had expressed a desire to reach an employment or educational goal." killackey2019 also states: "we believe that the recruited sample was representative of the population of individuals with FEP seeking employment."
employment_selection_source: killackey2019, Method, Participants, p. 76 and Results, Representativeness, p. 77; clarke2023, Materials and methods, Participants, p. 771

cohort_name: Chicago Follow-up Study (Chicago Longitudinal Research Program)
diagnostic_instrument: DSM-III, with the Schedule for Affective Disorders and Schizophrenia (SADS), the Schizophrenia State Inventory and collateral information at index hospitalisation; inter-rater kappa 0.88 for the schizophrenia sample
diagnosis_confirmed: research diagnostic assessment during the index hospitalisation by trained raters
overlap_notes: Described by harrow2017 (139 patients: 70 schizophrenia, 69 psychotic mood disorder) and jones2024 (256 patients aged 32 or under with a psychotic disorder and at least one follow-up). The two analysis samples are drawn from the same recruited cohort and overlap; their figures must never be pooled. recruitment_start is the study initiation year given by jones2024 ('The CLRP was initiated in 1970 at two urban hospitals'); no recruitment window is stated in either report and recruitment_end is therefore blank.
employment_selection_verbatim: harrow2017: "Within the limits of studying relatively young patients, the participants were consecutive admissions to two Chicago-area hospitals (a private hospital and a state hospital) and all but 3 were between the ages of 17 and 32 years of age (mean age = 22.9 years)... All patients with schizophrenia selected for inclusion met the 6 month duration of illness criterion (none were schizophreniform patients)." jones2024: "The current study included all individuals <=32 years old diagnosed with a psychotic disorder and one or more follow-up (n = 256)." Neither report states any employment-related eligibility, enrolment or analytic restriction; the stated criteria are diagnostic, age-based and follow-up-based only.
employment_selection_source: harrow2017, Method, p. 268; jones2024, Methods, Parent study and Sub-sample, p. 2446

cohort_name: unnamed: psychiatry out-patient department, Regional Mental Hospital, Pune, Maharashtra, India
diagnostic_instrument: medical-record diagnosis of schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, bipolar disorder or major depression; no standardised diagnostic instrument was used
diagnosis_confirmed: not confirmed by research assessment; khare2022b lists 'the lack of standardized measures to assess diagnosis and symptoms' as a limitation (p. 244)
overlap_notes: Described by khare2022b (employment article) and khare2022 (cognition companion). Recruitment years are not stated in either report. subgroup_extractable = no: 90 per cent of the sample is schizophrenia-schizoaffective, but NO employment count is reported for a psychosis-only subgroup in either report, so a psychosis subgroup cannot be pulled out. khare2022 ran sensitivity analyses restricted to schizophrenia-schizoaffective participants but reported only cognition-work associations, no employment counts.
employment_selection_verbatim: "Inclusion criteria for the study were: (a) diagnosis of schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, bipolar disorder, or major depression; (b) age from 18 to 60 years; (c) verbally fluent in Marathi language; (d) residing in Pune district and receiving outpatient services at the Regional Mental Hospital, Pune; and (e) willing and able to provide informed consent." The identical five-item list appears in khare2022. No employment-related criterion appears in either, the participant flow diagram accounts for all 190 referrals, and the analysed denominator is defined by follow-up completion, not by work status.
employment_selection_source: khare2022b, Method, Participants, p. 238 and Figure 1, p. 239; khare2022, Method 2.1 Participants, p. 2

cohort_name: Suffolk County Mental Health Project
diagnostic_instrument: SCID for DSM-III-R at baseline, 6 months and 2 years; SCID for DSM-IV at year 10; longitudinal DSM-IV consensus diagnosis
diagnosis_confirmed: Consensus DSM-IV diagnosis reached by study psychiatrists from the SCIDs, medical record information and interviews with significant others; the 10-year diagnosis was used
overlap_notes: Cohort entry required a psychotic disorder at first admission, so 100% of the recruited cohort has a qualifying diagnosis. The reports in this batch analyse only participants whose 10-year consensus diagnosis was schizophrenia/schizoaffective disorder or bipolar disorder, excluding psychotic depression, substance-related and 'other' psychoses; the schizophrenia/schizoaffective subgroup is reported separately (146 of 233 in strassnig2018, 80 of 128 in strassnig2017). Other Suffolk County reports (Kotov 2017, Velthorst 2016) are not in this batch.
employment_selection_verbatim: Baseline inclusion criteria were age 15-60 years, residence in Suffolk County NY, and psychosis not due to a medical condition or substance abuse; exclusion criteria were a psychiatric hospitalization more than 6 months before the index admission, low intellectual ability (IQ < 70), incapacity to provide informed consent, and being a non-English speaker.
employment_selection_source: strassnig2018, Methods, p. 3 of the author manuscript (Schizophr Res 2018;197:150-155); the same criteria appear at strassnig2017, section 2 Methods, p. 181

cohort_name: unnamed: therapeutic community, Yuli Hospital, Hualien, Taiwan, 2013 to 2015
diagnostic_instrument: DSM-IV-TR schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder
diagnosis_confirmed: Clinical DSM-IV-TR diagnosis from hospital records; PANSS rated at enrolment by four board-certified psychiatrists (wang2020c) with reported interrater reliability (ICC 0.86-0.95)
overlap_notes: wang2020b (n=561) and wang2020c (n=525 in the abstract and results, 550 in the methods) describe the same therapeutic community over the same recruitment window (January 2013 to December 2015) with the same diagnostic inclusion, so they are one cohort with overlapping analysis samples. wang2020c also states that its baseline background data came from a shared dataset with a PSP validation study of 655 stable schizophrenia patients (Wu et al. 2013), which is not on the screening list.
employment_selection_verbatim: The participants received occupational rehabilitation in three types of employment, including 1) the hospital-based workshop (N = 323), which provides simple and repeated activities to develop work potential in patients with stable psychiatric symptoms; 2) sheltered employment (N = 68), which provides a protective workplace for patients with work potential who cannot work in a competitive workplace [...]; and 3) supported employment (N = 134), which has been highly effective for patients to achieve competitive employment in regular employment in an integrated community setting.
employment_selection_source: wang2020c, Methods, 'Initial type of employment', p. 4 (525 of 525 allocated to one of the three streams); corroborated by wang2020b, Methods section 2.1, p. 376, 'The patients in the therapeutic community at the hospital had greater access to occupational rehabilitation and worked outside the hospital while they were stable'

cohort_name: headspace Early Psychosis (hEP) programme, first-episode psychosis cohort
diagnostic_instrument: Comprehensive Assessment of At Risk Mental States (CAARMS; Yung et al. 2005) criteria for first-episode psychosis
diagnosis_confirmed: FEP status determined by hEP clinicians against the CAARMS criteria at entry to the service
overlap_notes: One of two parallel samples in andersen2024. The other, headspace_hep_uhr_au (n=1515), has a mutually exclusive prospectively applied entry definition (UHR rather than FEP per CAARMS), a different programme duration (6-12 months against 2-5 years) and is analysed separately throughout, so the two are separate cohorts under D12.5. Taken together the two samples are 1574 of 3089 (51.0%) qualifying. brown2022 reports the same service but is off the screening list under D10.1 and nothing was imported from it.
employment_selection_verbatim: The study sample is a naturalistic cohort of young people aged 12-25 accessing treatment for FEP or UHR through the hEP programme. [...] All young people accessing the service between 19 June 2017 and 22 March 2021 who consented to having their data used for service evaluation purposes were included in the current study.
employment_selection_source: andersen2024, Methods, Participants, pp. 876-877. Vocational support (including embedded IPS workers) is a component of the care delivered, not a condition of entry: 'all programmes ensure there is a focus on education and employment for young people wishing to address these goals' (Methods, Setting, p. 876)

cohort_name: headspace Early Psychosis (hEP) programme, ultra-high-risk cohort
diagnostic_instrument: Comprehensive Assessment of At Risk Mental States (CAARMS; Yung et al. 2005) ultra-high-risk criteria
diagnosis_confirmed: UHR status determined by hEP clinicians against the CAARMS criteria at entry to the service
overlap_notes: Recorded so that the composition of andersen2024 is auditable. chr is barred from the primary estimand outright (SAP section 7). No psychosis subgroup is separable: the report does not identify which UHR participants transitioned to psychosis. No results extracted; the UHR figures are in Table 2, p. 880 if a CHR analysis is later added.
employment_selection_verbatim: All young people accessing the service between 19 June 2017 and 22 March 2021 who consented to having their data used for service evaluation purposes were included in the current study.
employment_selection_source: andersen2024, Methods, Participants, p. 877

cohort_name: unnamed: pooled Danish early-onset psychosis clinical cohorts (EOPC, Attention, DBUP, TEA), 1998 to 2016
diagnostic_instrument: ICD-10 F20-F29, F30.2, F31.2, F31.5, F32.3, F33.3, established with the K-SADS-PL or SCAN version 2.1
diagnosis_confirmed: Diagnostic interview (K-SADS-PL or SCAN 2.1) at baseline in each of the four clinical studies; ICD-10 categories printed in Table 1
overlap_notes: All 205 EOP participants had a first-episode ICD-10 psychosis diagnosis: F20 131 (63.9%), F21 10, F22 3, F23 3, F25 26, F28/F29 22, affective psychoses 10 (Table 1, p. 51). A schizophrenia subgroup is separately reportable (Table 3, p. 53: 57 of 127 in competitive employment or education). One constituent study, TEA, is a randomised antipsychotic tolerability and efficacy trial and all of its participants are included without reweighting. Healthy controls (n=199) are a comparison group and are not a psychosis cohort; no cohort row is created for them.
employment_selection_verbatim: The study sample consists of participants between 10 and 17 years of age (both inclusive) with first-episode EOP and age- and sex-matched HCs. [...] EOP participants were recruited from inpatient and outpatient psychiatric units in Denmark between year 1998 and 2016. [...] All participants with EOP or HCs from the clinical studies were included in the current register-based follow-up.
employment_selection_source: andersen2026, Methods section 2.1 Participants, p. 49. Note: the four constituent studies' own inclusion and exclusion criteria are summarised only in supplementary Table A.1, which is not in the article PDF; see unresolved_queries.md

cohort_name: unnamed: Institut Universitaire en Sante Mentale de Montreal (IUSMM) East-end Montreal first-admission incidence cohort, 1983-1987
diagnostic_instrument: DSM-III-R schizophrenia, applied at chart review of all first admissions
diagnosis_confirmed: chart review by study psychiatrists at T1 and re-verified against the inclusion criteria at the 10-16 year follow-up, when 3 of 145 were removed as not first-episode
overlap_notes: Same participants as Nicole 1992 (T1) and Abdel-Baki 2011 (T3); neither is in the frozen screening set.
employment_selection_verbatim: The subjects included in this cohort fulfilled the following criteria: - First lifetime psychiatric admission to IUSMM between 1983 and 1987. - Living in the catchment area of the IUSMM. - Aged 18 years or older. - DSM-III-R diagnosis of schizophrenia. | No employment-related criterion appears in the list, and the recruitment pathway is a first psychiatric hospitalisation in a sectorised catchment area, which cannot condition on employment. Fuller criteria are cited to two earlier reports ('Inclusion and exclusion criteria as well as methodological details on diagnostic procedure are further detailed in two previous articles') and are not reproduced here, so the classification rests on the criteria as printed. The restriction of occupational data to patients still followed by the catchment-area service is loss of ascertainment, not employment selection (D12.3c).
employment_selection_source: Method, Sample, p. 1320

cohort_name: unnamed: VA Connecticut Healthcare System and Connecticut Mental Health Center vocational rehabilitation trial sample (NCT00829400), 2009-2015
diagnostic_instrument: Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-IV (SCID)
diagnosis_confirmed: SCID administered at baseline for diagnostic evaluation
overlap_notes: Recruitment years are given as the data-collection span ('Data collection was begun in 2009 and completed in 2015'); no separate recruitment window is printed. 13 of the 77 participants came from CMHC after the study was widened in its third year to meet recruitment goals, under the same criteria and the same randomisation, so this is one cohort.
employment_selection_verbatim: Inclusion criteria included willingness to engage in vocational rehabilitation services of some kind and presence of disabling psychotic illness. Additionally, vocational programs had some admission requirements including demonstrated need for services, referral from clinicians, and an interest in work rehabilitation. All participants were unemployed, though a few were earning money through informal work. | Corroborated by 'Seventy-seven participants including 64 Veterans at VA Connecticut Healthcare System (VACHS) and 13 non-veterans at Connecticut Mental Health Center (CMHC) with chronic and disabling psychotic illness ... in transitional work services (45.5%) or supported employment (54.5%) were included in the study.' Four D9 triggers are present at once: vocational-service entry (every participant was an entrant to a transitional-work or supported-employment programme), work intention or readiness ('willingness to engage in vocational rehabilitation services', 'an interest in work rehabilitation'), baseline employment status ('All participants were unemployed') and current placement (at baseline 24 'had just begun working in Incentive Therapy', 6 'had begun working in Compensated Work Therapy' and 2 'were working casual jobs a few hours a week'). employment_selection_reason records vocational_service_entry as the primary classification because it applies to the whole sample by design.
employment_selection_source: Method, Participants, p. 6; corroborated Results, Sample Characteristics, p. 2

cohort_name: Prevention and Early Intervention Program for Psychoses (PEPP), London, Ontario
diagnostic_instrument: DSM-IV non-affective psychotic disorder
diagnosis_confirmed: programme clinical diagnosis; a DSM-IV non-affective psychotic disorder was an eligibility criterion for the follow-up study
overlap_notes: PEPP London also generates mackinley2022 (not in the frozen screening set). The authors describe the present work as 'a secondary analysis of data' from the PEPP long-term follow-up study; report_cohort_map records `describes` because the 10-year occupational and employment counts appear here.
employment_selection_verbatim: Participants were clients of the Prevention and Early Intervention Program for Psychoses (PEPP; London, Canada), admitted for initial treatment of a first episode of psychosis between March 1997 and February 2002 who agreed to participate in a long-term follow-up study. ... Participation in the current study was restricted to clients for whom at least 10 years had elapsed since receiving initial treatment for FEP and who fulfilled the following eligibility criteria: (1) ability to speak or understand English; (2) competent and willing to provide written informed consent; (3) diagnosed with a non-affective psychotic disorder that meets Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fourth Edition (DSM-IV) criteria; and (4) current outpatient status. | The eligibility list is stated exhaustively and contains no employment-related criterion. The PEPP programme's own admission criteria are cited to refs 57 and 58 ('The program inclusion criteria, assessment, and treatment protocol are described in detail elsewhere') and are not reproduced, so the classification rests on the criteria as printed; this is flagged for Stage G verification in unresolved_queries.md.
employment_selection_source: Methods, Study participants, p. 172

cohort_name: unnamed: NIMH Intramural Research Program Clinical and Translational Neuroscience Branch schizophrenia research volunteers, recontacted by telephone
diagnostic_instrument: Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-IV (SCID) administered by two clinicians at the initial visit
diagnosis_confirmed: SCID by two clinicians, with history, physical examination, blood work, urine toxicology and structural MRI to determine eligibility
overlap_notes: Recruitment years are not reported. The cohort is assembled from participants of earlier CTNB protocols (NCT00001247, NCT00001486); the source sample size is not reported, so the proportion recontacted cannot be computed.
employment_selection_verbatim: Researchers attempted to contact via phone people with schizophrenia spectrum disorder who had volunteered in a Clinical and Translational Neuroscience Branch (CTNB) study at the National Institute of Mental Health (NIMH) Intramural Research Program at the National Institutes of Health (NIH) for follow-up. 124 individuals were able to be contacted based on the contact information they provided at their initial visit and agreed to participate in the follow-up phone interview. ... In addition, participants completed a history and physical examination, routine blood work, urine toxicology, and structural brain MRI (reviewed by a radiologist) to determine eligibility for the study. Individuals who had substantial chronic medical, neurological, or substance use conditions were excluded. | No employment-related criterion operates at recruitment. The separate removal of 4 participants who reported being 'retired' restricts the ANALYSED DENOMINATOR rather than recruitment, and is recorded at arm level as analysis_selection_status = selected (analytic_restriction), following the convention set for mihaljevicpeles2016. The parent CTNB protocols' full eligibility criteria are not reproduced here.
employment_selection_source: Methods 2.1 Participants, p. 2

cohort_name: CROSS-TRACKS first-episode psychotic disorder cohort, Central Denmark Region
diagnostic_instrument: ICD-10 F20-F29 register diagnosis in the Danish National Patient Registry
diagnosis_confirmed: register diagnosis only; no clinical re-interview. The authors note diagnostic instability between schizophrenia and other psychotic disorders over time
overlap_notes: Regional (Central Denmark Region) subset of the Danish national registers, so participants may also appear in whole-country Danish register cohorts in this review. The title calls the study a 'population-based national registry study' while the Methods restrict it to the Central Region.
employment_selection_verbatim: The study population included individuals who were alive and eligible for labor market or educational participation. Therefore, individuals receiving disability pension at baseline (i.e. at the time of psychotic diagnosis) were excluded. | The exclusion is part of the definition of the study population, not only of an analysis: Fig. 1 removes 'On disability pension at time of diagnosis, n=35' from the 2,633 identified before the cohort eligible for follow-up (n=2,598) is formed. Disability pension at baseline is a labour-market status, and the excluded group is by definition not employed, so the restriction conditions the cohort on employment-related grounds under D9.
employment_selection_source: Methods, Study design and population; Fig. 1 flow chart

cohort_name: First Episode Psychosis Outcome Study (FEPOS), Early Psychosis Prevention and Intervention Centre (EPPIC), Melbourne
diagnostic_instrument: DSM-IV, consensus clinical diagnoses derived from the medical file with the Early Psychosis File Questionnaire (EPFQ)
diagnosis_confirmed: consensus diagnostic process over the whole treatment period, extracted from files by two senior psychiatrists; 43 patients with a non-psychotic diagnosis at endpoint were excluded
overlap_notes: Same 661 FEPOS patients as Conus 2007 (ref 21) and the 643 of Lambert 2005 (ref 22). A 15-year follow-up of this cohort was under way at the time of publication.
employment_selection_verbatim: The initial sample comprised a population-based cohort of 786 FEP patients consecutively admitted to EPPIC in Melbourne between 1998 and 2000. At the time of the study, EPPIC was mandated to treat all FEP patients aged 15-29 in the catchment area with little if any leakage to private psychiatrists; as such, the study sample represents a treated epidemiological cohort. The files of 82 patients (10%) had been sent to other services at time of discharge and were not available for the study; these patients did not differ regarding diagnostic distribution and available demographic characteristics. Among 704 available files, 43 were excluded because of a non-psychotic diagnosis at endpoint. Data on 661 patients were analyzed. | The only exclusions are file unavailability and a non-psychotic diagnosis; no employment-related criterion appears. The cohort was assembled by file audit without an informed-consent procedure, which the authors present as the reason it avoids the refusal-based selection of comparable samples.
employment_selection_source: Methods, Patients sample, p. 1090

cohort_name: Employment Intervention Demonstration Program (EIDP)
diagnostic_instrument: DSM-IV axis I diagnosis of mental illness; instrument not named in this report
diagnosis_confirmed: not described in this report
overlap_notes: Eight sites in four US regions; 1,648 enrolled. This report analyses 449 from six sites. detore2019's Hartford trial is one of the eight EIDP sites (its acknowledgements name EIDP cooperative agreement UD7 SM51818), so eidp_usa and hartford_ips_rct may share participants and must not be pooled.
employment_selection_verbatim: Participants met the following study inclusion criteria: age 18 years or older; having a DSM-IV axis I diagnosis of mental illness; desiring employment; being unemployed (except at one site); and providing informed consent. | Corroborated (Discussion, p. 1013): 'the study population consisted of paid volunteer subjects who were interested in working, a group that may not be representative of the broader population of individuals with psychiatric disabilities.' | Coded work_intention_or_readiness rather than baseline_employment_status because 'desiring employment' applied at every site whereas the unemployment requirement carried a stated exception at one site; both are employment-related restrictions.
employment_selection_source: Method, EIDP description, p. 1008; corroborated in Discussion limitations, p. 1013

cohort_name: Hartford study of supported employment (Capitol Regional Mental Health Center)
diagnostic_instrument: Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-IV (SCID); severe mental illness as defined by the State of Connecticut Department of Mental Health and Addiction Services
diagnosis_confirmed: SCID administered by trained interviewers
overlap_notes: One of the eight Employment Intervention Demonstration Program sites (acknowledgements, cooperative #UD7 SM51818), so participants overlap the EIDP cohort eidp_usa reported by cook2016. Possible but unevidenced overlap with ct_dual_diagnosis (drake2015), same city and era.
employment_selection_verbatim: Inclusion criteria for the study were: (1) a severe mental illness as defined by the State of Connecticut Department of Mental Health and Addiction Services (2) not employed at start of study; (3) interested in competitive employment; (4) attendance at two or more research introduction groups aimed at explaining the purposes and methods of the study; and (5) willing and legally able to provide informed consent. | Two employment-related restrictions apply without exception: baseline unemployment (criterion 2) and interest in competitive employment (criterion 3). The analysed sample of this report is restricted further, to the 51 of 68 IPS participants 'who obtained a competitive job during the study period'.
employment_selection_source: Method 2.1 Participants, p. 313; analysis restriction stated in Method overview, p. 313

cohort_name: Ferrara early intervention service first-episode psychosis programme
diagnosis_confirmed: clinical diagnosis recorded in the electronic health record; CHR individuals excluded
overlap_notes: Emilia-Romagna regional FEP programme; the authors' earlier Ferrara cohort reports draw on the same service. Design coded retrospective_cohort because the data were assembled from electronic health records for admissions from 2012 under an ethics approval granted in October 2021, although the HoNOS follow-ups were administered prospectively as routine care and the authors describe the study as 'a longitudinal cohort study'.
employment_selection_verbatim: Patients were those admitted to the EIS in Ferrara between 2012 and February 27th, 2025 who met the following enrolment criteria: (a) diagnosed with affective or non-affective FEP; (b) not being treated for more than 24 months; (c) absence of intellectual disability; (d) aged between 18 and 35 years; (e) absence of organic psychosis. | No employment-related criterion appears in the enrolment criteria or in Figure 1's exclusions (no psychosis diagnosis n = 29, CHR diagnosis n = 11, age range n = 18). Employment was measured, not required: 'Employed (yes) 63 (36.2)' at admission (Table 1), so 64% were not employed at entry and were retained.
employment_selection_source: Abstract Methods, p. 1 and Methods 2.2 Participants, p. 3; exclusions in Figure 1, p. 4; baseline employment in Table 1, p. 5

cohort_name: Connecticut (CT) Dual Diagnosis Study
diagnostic_instrument: Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-III-R
diagnosis_confirmed: clinician research interviewers established diagnoses of mental and substance use disorders
overlap_notes: 198 enrolled in a randomised trial of assertive community treatment against standard clinical case management, both delivering integrated mental health and substance abuse treatment; the two arms were merged after the 3-year trial for a 4-year naturalistic follow-up. This report analyses only the 150 with schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder. Possible but unevidenced overlap with hartford_ips_rct.
employment_selection_verbatim: Participants in the initial trial met the following inclusion criteria: major psychotic disorder (schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, bipolar disorder, or major depression with psychotic features); active substance use disorder (abuse or dependence on alcohol or other drugs within the past 6 months); high service use in the past 2 years (2 or more of the following: psychiatric hospitalizations, stays in a psychiatric crisis or respite program, emergency department visits, or incarcerations); homelessness or unstable housing; poor independent living skills; no pending legal charges, life-threatening medical conditions, or mental retardation; being scheduled for discharge to community living if currently staying in an inpatient facility; and willingness to provide written informed consent. | None of these is an employment-related criterion. The cohort is heavily selected on clinical and social criteria (substance use, service use, housing, living skills), which D9 does not treat as employment selection, and baseline employment was measured rather than required ('Competitive job past y (yes) 20 14%' at baseline, Table 3).
employment_selection_source: Methods, Study Group, p. 203; baseline employment in Table 3, p. 207

cohort_name: Stockholm County first-time non-affective psychosis cases 2005/2006
diagnostic_instrument: ICD-10 F20-F29 recorded in the Stockholm County Psychiatric Care System (PVS) register
diagnosis_confirmed: validated register diagnosis from in- and outpatient psychiatric care; no clinical re-interview
overlap_notes: PVS covers 75% of the adult population of Stockholm County. Incidence is register-defined (no earlier inpatient registration since 1973, no earlier outpatient registration since 1997) rather than a clinically confirmed first episode, which is why first_episode is coded yes with that qualification. Check against other Swedish register cohorts (stockholm_2000, se_registers) before pooling.
employment_selection_verbatim: The study population consisted of residents (aged 18-44) in the five catchment areas covered by the PVS. We identified 756 first time cases diagnosed with non-affective psychosis registered in in- and outpatient psychiatric care in 2005 or 2006 (inclusion years). These cases had no earlier registration of the diagnosis in inpatient psychiatric care since 1973 or outpatient psychiatric care since 1997. ... Due to exclusion criteria, persons who were deceased during inclusion year or migrated from or to Sweden at inclusion or 5 years prior to inclusion were excluded. | No employment-related criterion appears in the population definition or the exclusions.
employment_selection_source: Materials and methods, Study population, p. 260

cohort_name: Recovery After an Initial Schizophrenia Episode - Early Treatment Program (RAISE-ETP)
diagnostic_instrument: Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-IV (SCID); schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, schizophreniform disorder, brief psychotic disorder or psychotic disorder not otherwise specified
diagnosis_confirmed: centralised remote raters blind to study design and assignment, by two-way video conferencing
overlap_notes: 404 participants at 34 community mental health treatment centres in 21 states. Any other RAISE-ETP or NAVIGATE report shares these participants.
employment_selection_verbatim: Four hundred four participants between the ages of 15 and 40 were recruited across 34 community mental health treatment centers in 21 states and were followed up for a minimum of 2 years. ... Individuals were eligible if they had one of the following DSM-IV diagnoses: SZ, schizoaffective disorder, schizophreniform disorder, brief psychotic disorder, or psychotic disorder not otherwise specified. Individuals with clinically significant head trauma or other serious medical conditions were excluded. All participants had experienced only a single episode of psychosis and had <=6 months of lifetime antipsychotic medication treatment. | No employment-related criterion appears in the eligibility list, and 39.8% were in work or school at baseline, so people out of work were enrolled. The report refers to the parent trial for fuller recruitment procedures, but the eligibility list it prints is complete on its face and contains no employment element, so `none` rather than `unclear`.
employment_selection_source: Methods, Participants, p. 370; baseline work-or-school in Table 1, p. 371

cohort_name: Early Youth Engagement (EYE-2) trial
diagnostic_instrument: No research diagnostic instrument. Eligibility was acceptance by an NHS England early intervention in psychosis service, i.e. 'meeting FEP service criteria'; 40% of referrals (1525 patients) were assessed by the teams as not having first-episode psychosis and excluded
diagnosis_confirmed: EIP team clinical assessment against NICE-concordant service criteria, recorded in routine NHS data; no independent verification is reported
overlap_notes: 20 EIP teams at five NHS sites (nine trusts) in England, approximately 10% of new FEP patients in England in the period. Consecutive referrals mid-May 2019 to mid-July 2020.
employment_selection_verbatim: Patient inclusion criteria were: consecutive referrals between mid-May 2019 and mid-July 2020; aged 14-35 years; and meeting FEP service criteria. No consent was required for the main trial, which used de-identified, routine data. All patients were therefore included. | Service inclusion criteria were: stand-alone service with at least two discrete teams; accepting at least 35-40 new FEP cases annually; collecting NHS England-mandated routine outcomes; geographic and population variation. | No employment, vocational or work-motivation criterion appears in either list, and because no patient consent was required for the main trial there was no self-selection at entry either. The socio-occupational analysis is restricted to the 232 who consented to the societal cost-effectiveness interview, which is a consent-based analytic restriction and not an employment-related one (D12.3c).
employment_selection_source: Method, Cluster and participant eligibility, p. 145

cohort_name: unnamed: Danish national registers, 1955-1991 birth cohort with schizophrenia first diagnosed between ages 15 and 25
diagnostic_instrument: ICD-10 F20; ICD-8 295.x9 excluding 295.79 (schizoaffective disorder), recorded in the Danish Psychiatric Central Research Register on a psychiatric admission, outpatient contact or psychiatric emergency visit
diagnosis_confirmed: Register diagnosis only; the authors cite Uggerby 2013 for good validity of the schizophrenia diagnosis in this register and note that a small percentage are mistakenly registered
overlap_notes: recruitment_start and recruitment_end are deliberately BLANK: there is no recruitment window in the survey sense. The population is a birth cohort (1 January 1955 to 31 December 1991) alive at its 25th birthday; schizophrenia had to be first diagnosed between ages 15 and 25, and outcomes were measured annually from 1980 to 2016 at ages 25 to 61. Recording the birth years in a recruitment field would let them be read as a recruitment era moderator.
employment_selection_verbatim: Our study population included all individuals born in Denmark between January 1, 1955 and December 31, 1991, who were alive at their 25th birthday. | Individuals were defined as having schizophrenia (ICD-10 code F20; ICD-8 codes 295.x9 [excluding 295.79 (schizoaffective disorder)]) if they had been admitted to a psychiatric hospital, had received outpatient psychiatric care, or had visited psychiatric emergency unit. | Whole-population register linkage with no consent, no recruitment and no analytic restriction on employment. The design cannot condition on employment, and employment is the outcome rather than an eligibility criterion.
employment_selection_source: Materials and methods, Study population and Schizophrenia assessment, p. 1344

cohort_name: unnamed: all individuals first hospitalised for schizophrenia (ICD-10 F20) in Finland, 1988-2015
diagnostic_instrument: ICD-10 F20 as the primary diagnosis of the first hospitalisation recorded in the Finnish Hospital Discharge Register
diagnosis_confirmed: Register diagnosis only; the authors cite Makikyro 1998 for good validity of the register schizophrenia diagnosis and note that diagnoses are usually made over a hospitalisation of several weeks by several psychiatrists
overlap_notes: One of three case groups separately ascertained in this report; the others are other nonaffective psychosis (fi_registers_nonaff) and bipolar disorder (not extracted). The groups cannot share participants: 'Only data from the first such hospitalization and primary diagnoses were used, and thus an individual was categorized only into one diagnostic group'.
